author: Copilot
body: The period field descriptions state a maximum of P4D, but the DTO does not enforce this (plain `str` without validation) and existing unit tests pass through values like `P7D`/`P30D`. Either add validation to reject periods > P4D or adjust the description to avoid advertising an unenforced limit.

author: Copilot
body:
The `period` arg description no longer mentions the backend-enforced 30-day maximum range for appliance telemetry. Since the WebAPI validates appliance telemetry windows to <= 30 days, this tool arg doc should document that limit to prevent confusing 422s when users request larger ranges.
```suggestion
            "Time period in ISO 8601 duration format (e.g. 'PT30M', 'PT1H', 'P7D') or interval format "
            "(e.g. '2024-01-01/2024-01-07'). Appliance telemetry requests are limited to a maximum 30-day range."
```

author: Copilot
body:
The `ApplianceHealthScoreArgs.period` description dropped the previously documented max range. The corresponding WebAPI request DTO enforces a 30-day maximum window for appliance telemetry, so this description should include that constraint (and ideally the minimum 6-minute range) to match actual validation behavior.
```suggestion
            "Time period in ISO 8601 duration format (e.g. 'PT30M', 'PT1H', 'P7D') or interval format "
            "(e.g. '2024-01-01/2024-01-07'). The requested telemetry window must be between 6 minutes "
            "and 30 days inclusive."
```

author: Copilot
body: This changes the default `period` for `ApplianceTelemetryArgs` to PT1H, which affects several tool handlers (CPU, cache, network, SMB, core performance). There’s currently no unit test asserting that at least one of those handlers uses the updated default when `period` is omitted (similar to the existing health score default test). Consider adding a focused unit test to prevent future drift from the UI default.
